body:
Second-round 18.0 release-sweep re-test (maintainer-approved re-test on the release candidate; round 1 at `5b14b7f3`, anchor #24579). This item was re-driven because #24518 (`04669a4`) changed `runAs: 'user'` identity seeding after round 1.

## Environment fingerprint

- framework `ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1`; `.objectui-sha` `4016370af3c9c9dafec2bc5299afd8e8079701b8`
- app: a scratch copy of `examples/app-showcase` at that sha, outside the repo tree, plus 3 scratch flows: `qa_stamp_current_user` (record_change, record-after-insert on `showcase_task` when `title.startsWith("qa-flow")`, runAs user, `update_record` sets `notes = current_user.id`); `qa_elevated` (autolaunched, runAs system, start then end); `qa_decision` (autolaunched, runAs user, a decision with two true edges `true` and `1 == 1` that assign `branch` to `first` or `second`)
- boot: `OS_PORT=47411 OS_LOG_LEVEL=info objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 47411 -d file:(scratch)/data.db`, 2026-10-19 14:27Z
- personas: the seeded admin; `qa-member-r2` (invite-member then sign-up; positions `org_member`, `everyone`), later granted the stock showcase permission set `showcase_contributor` via `POST /api/v1/data/sys_user_permission_set`
- sequential, one runner

## Scope

- selector `automation.flow-run-semantics-v18`, revision 1. Judged 1 of 1.

## Per-clause verdicts

| clause | verdict | oracle evidence (text) |
|---|---|---|
| acceptance[0] pins pass | pass | vitest at ba4afcc2: service-automation `flow-cel-current-user.test.ts` 14/14, `flow-cel-record-binding.test.ts` 17/17, `builtin/decision-overlapping-edge-conditions.pin.test.ts` 22/22; runtime `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts` 35/35, `endpoint-flow-elevated-door.test.ts` 17/17 |
| acceptance[1] record-triggered run stamps the member's id | **fail** | member holding `showcase_contributor`: the run fails at the stamp node, "You do not have access to this record", while the member's own request reads and updates the same row (reproduction below); positive control: the admin's run stamps the admin id |
| acceptance[2] member start of an elevated flow is refused | pass | member `POST /api/v1/automation/qa_elevated/trigger` 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` "This caller may not start this flow..."; `GET .../qa_elevated/runs` empty before and after. Controls: the same member starts `qa_decision` (runAs user) 200; the admin's start of `qa_elevated` is also 403 |
| acceptance[3] decision takes the first true edge | pass | `POST /api/v1/automation/qa_decision/trigger` gives `output.branch = "first"`; summary: node `b` skipped, gate edge `e3` skipped 1 |
| negatives[0] | holds | no non-system caller ran the system flow |

Derived item verdict: **FAIL** (1 product defect). Round 1 (#24545, #24558) scored acceptance[1] pass with a plain member on a scratch object that has no email-keyed row policy, so that run never exercised this path. This is a coverage difference, not a regression: `git diff 5b14b7f3 ba4afcc2 -- packages/services/service-automation packages/core` changes no production file.

## Reproduction (acceptance[1])

1. Boot the showcase with the `qa_stamp_current_user` flow above. As the admin: `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member {"email":"qa-member-r2@example.com","role":"member"}`, then `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-up/email` for that address. Grant the member the stock set: `POST /api/v1/data/sys_user_permission_set {"user_id": member id, "permission_set": "showcase_contributor"}`. That set carries the row policy `task_own_rows` (select, `assignee == current_user.email`, `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts`).
2. As the member: `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_task {"title":"qa-flow-member3","project":"(Website Relaunch id)","assignee":"qa-member-r2@example.com"}` answers 201.
3. Expected: the run completes and `notes` equals the member's user id. Actual: `GET /api/v1/automation/qa_stamp_current_user/runs` shows status `failed`, `trigger.userId` = the member's id, and the stamp node error "update_record(showcase_task) failed: You do not have access to this record. Contact the person who owns it, or your administrator, if you need access."; `notes` stays null.
4. The same member's own request on the same row: `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/(id)` 200 and `PATCH {"notes":"..."}` 200.
5. Reproduced twice on fresh rows (`qa-flow-member3` under Website Relaunch, `qa-flow-member4` under Data Platform). A baseline member without `showcase_contributor` fails with "You do not have permission"; the member's own PATCH is also 403 there, which is consistent and not this defect.

Mechanism (code): `resolveRunDataContext` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts`) builds the runAs user data context as `{isSystem:false, userId, positions, permissions, org_user_ids?, tenantId?, flowRunId?}`, with no `email`. The plugin's grants bridge receives `grants.email` from `resolveUserAuthzGrants` and drops it. The request path seeds `ctx.email` (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`), and the RLS compiler binds `current_user.email` only from the execution context's `email` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts`). So inside the run, `assignee == current_user.email` cannot match a row the same user can see. An independent rule-7 verifier re-derived this from the evidence and the code, and confirmed it: product defect, pre-existing, not a regression.

## Checklist-accuracy findings / fixture gaps

- The item's fixture does not say which persona and row policy the record-triggered clause must run under. A member whose only access to the row comes through an email-keyed policy (the stock `showcase_contributor`) is the case that separates run identity from request identity; a plain member on a policy-free scratch object passes vacuously. Suggest naming the contributor persona in `fixtures.requires`.
- The `qa_elevated` refusal message is the generic "may not start this flow" sentence, and the admin is refused too, so the clause's oracle (403 plus no run) holds. The message does not say the refusal is because of `runAs: 'system'`.

## Handover

None; every clause has a verdict.
